justifications.c1: Direct losses are small: £270 per valve (Islington via Inside Housing, search-confirmed) and £3,500 for 32 valves across two Aberdeen blocks (~£109/valve; P&J reports it as equipment value, replacement wording unconfirmed); the life-safety exposure is unpriced and loss per riser is below 5× the cost of 16+ tags plus subscription.
justifications.c2: Thefts come in unpredictable clusters (Bristol 11 blocks in a month, Aberdeen, Birmingham, Stevenage) with no per-block rate, but FS(E)R 2022 reg 7 mandates a monthly routine check of essential fire-fighting equipment including rising mains (search-confirmed).
justifications.c3: Documented routines: six-monthly visual and annual wet tests (2017 council tender), £400–£1,200 per system per year (pricing guide, not a quote), PTSG call-outs, security patrols, welding/bolting; labour of the in-house monthly reg 7 checks is not quantified.
justifications.c4: FS(E)R 2022 reg 7 requires monthly checks, a record accessible to residents and fault reporting to the FRS (search-confirmed via legislation.gov.uk and the Home Office fact sheet), but no enforcement for missing riser valves or reg 7 breaches was found and the rule is England-only.
justifications.c5: Building Safety Manager adverts (Peabody ~£57k, Camden) evidence a responsible job title for high-rise fire safety, but riser work is bought through formal public/HA tenders and budget authority is not shown.
justifications.c6: Riser test contractors (PTSG, Churches Fire) visit on six-monthly cycles and PTSG does anti-theft remedials (vendor sources), and Ealing bought IoT fire devices from FireAngel, but no riser contractor is shown selling remote monitoring.
justifications.c7: No comparable riser monitoring product or paying customer was found, and cheap one-off physical fixes (welding, bolts, shear nuts, cabinets, padlocks) already work: Islington reports 'a big drop in thefts' — a good-enough incumbent red flag.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN tilt and contact sensors cost $50–80 each, but a riser needs 16+ tags, and LoRa propagation up a concrete stair core is not evidenced.
justifications.c9: Reg 7 creates a statutory monthly record, but nothing shows automated monitoring satisfies it and no comparable subscription prices were found.
justifications.c10: Police appeals (Police Scotland), council press release (Royal Greenwich), trade press (Inside Housing, FIA), BMRA theft alert, local news in several regions and a Grenfell Inquiry exhibit; no first-hand resident or ombudsman complaints.

weakest: Cheap one-off physical hardening (welding, bolts, shear nuts) already cuts thefts and no one is shown paying for riser monitoring, while losses per incident are only a few hundred to a few thousand pounds.
